description: The identifier of a legal entity: a 20-character alphanumeric code that is unique and stands for one entity, so an organisation can be named across systems and checked against GLEIF's Global LEI Index (`schema:leiCode`). Proposed for B2B verification of organisations; no LEI is stored today.
versionCommitment: ISO 17442-1:2020 for the LEI and its assignment; ISO 17442-2:2020 for an LEI in a digital certificate
stewardOrganisation: ISO (ISO/TC 68/SC 8); the LEI system is run by GLEIF
usageNotes: Licence: the standard's text is sold by ISO (CHF 67 for Part 1; "(c) ISO" on the page) and no open licence for the text was found. The data is open: GLEIF's LEI Data Terms of Use (gleif.org/en/meta/lei-data-terms-of-use) say the data available through its access service "are provided under the CC0 licence", and GLEIF describes the LEI as "A public good, available free of charge to all users". Steward: ISO/TC 68/SC 8 is the responsible committee; GLEIF (Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation), a Swiss not-for-profit foundation incorporated by the Financial Stability Board, runs the system with the local operating units (LOUs) it accredits, under the Regulatory Oversight Committee. Scope: legal entities, including international branches and individuals acting in a business capacity (sole traders are an ISO example), and not natural persons. Schema.org has the property `leiCode` ("An organization identifier that uniquely identifies a legal entity as defined in ISO 17442"). Platform use: none yet; the entity model has `taxId`, `registrationNumber`, `gln` and `openCorporatesId` and no `leiCode` (audit 2026-10-07, nyuchi/data-infra#94). Added from nyuchi/data-infra#94 and #179.

description: Where a piece of media came from: captured, digitised, human-edited, algorithmically altered, composite, or made by a trained model. versionCommitment: Track the live vocabulary; store the concept URI (`http://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/<term>`), not a label
usageNotes: Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (the vocabulary page: "Copyright 2024 IPTC ... The Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY) 4.0 license applies to all NewsCodes"; the scheme's JSON names IPTC as copyright holder and links CC BY 4.0). It is data, not code. The scheme's own definition says "from which source a digital image was created" and the concept definitions say "media"; none of the 20 concept definitions names text, so using the codes for AI-made article text is the platform's application of them, not something IPTC states. C2PA 2.4 (c2pa) takes these URIs in its digitalSourceType field, and the ninjs 3.2 schema (iptc_ninjs) has a digitalSourceType property that suggests this vocabulary (both read 2026-11-11).
